question: Can an efficiently quantized tool-mode recurrent decoder trained on diverse typed functions execute independently authored numerical requests, ground its final answer in the returned value, and outperform untouched Base?
gate: Twenty-two consecutive public executable BFCL requests. At least five net additional exact argument paths with a numeric final answer within 0.5 percent of the local execution, two-sided paired p<=.05, no slower than Base. Record all argument, final answer, completion and memory outcomes. Failed gate closes deployment/matched attribution for this fit. If passed, test matched one-pass initialized with exactly the same quantized sibling and training, and confirm external schema transfer. Half of each publisher pair can share its schema; also report function-pair clusters descriptively.
protocol: Independent response to zero-valid-call BFCL transfer for catalog-only training. Fixed instruction-tuned Qwen sibling, 8-bit grouped quantization of all eligible embedding and linear weights outside the BF16 shared final layer. 384 unrelated typed training interactions over eight executable utilities, public read-only Glaive/Hermes demonstrations and 128 controlled turns. At test consume questions and schemas only, with identical shared tool instructions. Execute only declared local callbacks. No training examples from BFCL. Score only one correct typed call followed by completed numeric response. Equal policy and archived timing against unmodified BF16 pinned Base.
